raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou for more than fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this land. The soil here in the plain is good for wheat and corn — that is what we have always grown, and that is what I will grow again.

My family has about 7 mu. Every year since I was young, we plant winter wheat in October after the autumn rain, then come June after the harvest, we turn around and put in summer corn on the same ground. Two crops, same land, every year. I have never grown anything else for the main field. There is no reason to change now.

For seeds, I use whatever the village supply cooperative sells — they stopped selling the old seed a long time ago, everything is improved or hybrid now. I pay a little more but the yield is better, so I accept it.

For fertilizer, I put down a good amount of urea and diammonium phosphate when I plant, and top-dress the nitrogen in spring for wheat and at tasseling for corn. My neighbor puts down a bit less than me but his plants sometimes turn yellow, so I keep my amounts where they are. Potash I barely use — never really did, my father didn't either.

I water wheat four times: before the ground freezes in late autumn, again at jointing, at heading, and before grain fills. For corn I water less — summer rain usually helps, maybe twice. I use a rotary tiller before planting wheat. For corn I often just plant into the wheat stubble directly — saves time and my back is not what it was.

Pesticides I apply twice for wheat — once for aphids and once for the fungal disease that comes in wet springs. Corn usually only needs one treatment.

I expect about 450 jin of wheat per mu and 550 jin of corn per mu, which is what I have been getting most years.
